title: Which Velocity Is Real? Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A trip app says Aarav's ride averaged 12 km/h. His speedometer showed 25 on the slope and 0 at the signal. Three numbers, all true. So which one is his real velocity? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn the difference between average velocity over an interval and instantaneous velocity at one instant.

On a live motion notebook Aarav starts from rest with x = t². We shrink the time gap from 2 s to 0.01 s and watch the averages close in on 4 m/s while the chord on the x-t graph turns into the tangent. Then we derive v = lim Δx/Δt = dx/dt step by step, read velocities off the slope of an x-t graph, and test round trips and the top of a hump with two pause-and-think questions. A worked example, the exam trap about averaging two speeds, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 One ride, three readings
0:26 Average velocity over the whole trip
0:49 Live sim: from rest, x = t²
1:13 Shrink the gap: the averages close in on 4 m/s
1:44 The rule: v = dx/dt, step by step
2:26 Side by side + pause and think
3:02 Reading velocity off an x-t graph
3:33 Worked example: x = 4t² + 2t
4:11 Exam trap: the mean of two speeds
4:41 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:22 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Average and Instantaneous Acceleration. Velocity tells how fast position changes. What tells how fast velocity changes?
